summary: Enterprise AI model API aggregators let corporations consume foundation models (GPT, Claude, Llama, Gemini, Mistral, and more) through secure, governed APIs that keep prompts and data inside the customer's cloud boundary. As of 2026, the market is dominated by the three hyperscalers (AWS, Microsoft, Google), with data-platform vendors (Snowflake, Databricks) and specialists (IBM, Oracle, Cloudflare) carving out niches tied to where enterprise data already lives. There is no single winner — selection is driven by existing cloud contracts, data residency needs, and which models a company is standardizing on.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: inference runs within the customer's own cloud tenant/VPC so prompts, embeddings, and outputs never leave the governed environment or get used to train vendor models.

Compliance and governance: built-in audit logging, access controls (IAM/Entra ID), and certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, GDPR) that raw vendor APIs often do not provide out of the box.
Single billing and procurement: model usage flows through an existing cloud contract/committed spend, avoiding new vendor onboarding, legal review, and separate invoices for each model provider.
Model choice and avoiding lock-in: one API surface to access multiple model families (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Titan, Gemini, GPT) so teams can swap or benchmark models without re-architecting.
Enterprise integration and security: native connection to cloud identity, networking (private endpoints), secrets management, monitoring, and data services where corporate data already resides.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service
available_models: Models from Azure AI Foundry (Llama, Mistral, Cohere, Phi)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens by model, plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed through Azure.
key_features: Microsoft Entra ID identity and RBAC
Deep integration with Azure AI Foundry and Copilot stack
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardized on Microsoft/Azure that want first-party OpenAI (GPT) models with strong compliance and Office/Copilot integration.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Per-token on-demand pricing by model, plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; billed through AWS.
key_features: Guardrails for safety and PII redaction
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting the widest multi-vendor model choice (especially Claude) with native AWS security and agent tooling.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Per-token/per-character pricing by model, plus Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec); billed through Google Cloud.
key_features: VPC Service Controls and private endpoints
Grounding with Google Search and enterprise data
Strong MLOps via Vertex AI pipelines
platforms.best_for: Data/analytics-heavy enterprises on Google Cloud wanting Gemini plus a large open and third-party model catalog with mature MLOps.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx
platforms.pricing: Resource-unit (RU) and per-token consumption pricing; available on IBM Cloud, on-prem, and hybrid; subscription options.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk and audit
watsonx Orchestrate for enterprise AI agents
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises (banking, insurance, government) needing hybrid/on-prem deployment, governance, and IBM's agent orchestration.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits; LLM functions billed per token/credit within the data warehouse.
key_features: Models run inside Snowflake's governance perimeter — data never leaves
Role-based access control and data masking
Cortex Analyst and Cortex Search (RAG over governed data)
platforms.best_for: Organizations with data already in Snowflake wanting LLM analytics and RAG without moving data out of the warehouse.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
available_models: Open-source models via Foundation Model APIs
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs); pay-per-token Foundation Model APIs and provisioned throughput endpoints.
key_features: AI Gateway for routing and rate limiting across model providers
Fine-tuning and custom model training on your data
MLflow for model lifecycle and evaluation
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams wanting to fine-tune and build custom GenAI apps on top of their lakehouse with strong governance.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Per-character/per-token on-demand pricing, plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; billed through OCI.
key_features: Dedicated AI clusters for isolated inference
Integration with Oracle Fusion apps and Autonomous Database
Available in sovereign and government regions
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises (ERP/database customers) and sovereign cloud deployments wanting GenAI close to Oracle data.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use based on neurons/tokens; low-cost serverless pricing with generous free tier; billed through Cloudflare.
key_features: Serverless inference at the network edge (low latency, global)
AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, and observability across providers
Tight integration with Workers developer platform
platforms.best_for: Developers and companies building low-latency, globally distributed AI features at the edge, often with open-source models.
